summary: Will Smith spoke to fans at a Baltimore press event for Jada Pinkett Smith's memoir Worthy, calling their long marriage "tumultuous" and "brutiful" and crediting her sacrifices for his success. The comments follow Jada's revelations that the couple have been separated for seven years, though she later clarified they are working on healing and there is no divorce on paper.
one_line: Will Smith praised Jada Pinkett Smith at a Baltimore event for her memoir Worthy, describing their marriage as 'brutiful' amid separation revelations.
key_facts: Will Smith, 55, spoke at the Enoch Pratt Free Library in Baltimore, Maryland on 18 October at a press event for Jada Pinkett Smith's book Worthy.
Will and Jada married in 1997; their children Jaden (25) and Willow (22) attended the event.
Will described their relationship as "very, very long and tumultuous" and said they call it "brutiful" – brutal and beautiful at the same time.
Will called the marriage a "sloppy public experiment in unconditional love" and said he is "happier than [he's] ever been in [his] entire life."
Will said his dreams were "largely built on the foundation of Jada's sacrifices," noting she often put her career aside for his.
Will thanked Jada for her good relationship with his ex-wife Sheree Zampino, letting all three of his children grow up together; their 30-year-old son Trey Smith was also present.
Earlier that week Will posted an Instagram video titled "Official statement" in which he sneezed instead of giving an opinion.
Will told The New York Times that Jada's memoir "kind of woke him up" and that she is more "resilient, clever and compassionate than he'd understood."
In a People interview published on 10 October, Jada first revealed she and Will were living separately; her memoir says they have been separated for seven years.
On the Today show on 16 October, Jada told Hoda Kotb that they are "concentrating on healing" and that "There's no divorce on paper."
